conservation.help_by: Leave living plants where they grow; reduce nutrient runoff when you can.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t uproot algae or seagrass for aquariums without permits.

life_info.eating: Photosynthetic primary producer. Makes energy from sunlight (and sometimes from clear shallow water light).
life_info.mating: Spreads by spores, seeds, propagules, or creeping rhizomes depending on the species.
life_info.habitat: Reef flats and lagoons; jointed green coin-like segments. Forms habitat structure that shelters fish, crabs, and invertebrates.

fun_facts: Calcified segments break down into tropical white sand.
Looks like a string of underwater cactus pads.

conservation.help_by: Anchor in sand, not grass; support seagrass-friendly boat habits.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t drive propellers through meadows or dig up plants.

life_info.eating: Photosynthetic primary producer. Makes energy from sunlight (and sometimes from clear shallow water light).
life_info.mating: Spreads by spores, seeds, propagules, or creeping rhizomes depending on the species.
life_info.habitat: Aruba lagoons and seagrass beds — an introduced seagrass now mixed with native meadows. Forms habitat structure that shelters fish, crabs, and invertebrates.

fun_facts: Arrived in the Caribbean via the Suez–Atlantic route and now grows in Aruba MPAs.
Small oval leaves distinguish it from long-bladed turtle grass.

conservation.help_by: Keep nesting beaches dark and clear; support marine protected areas.
conservation.caution_against: Never buy turtle products; don’t block crawlways or touch nesting turtles.

life_info.eating: Sponges — one of the few animals that dine on them. Narrow beak reaches into reef cracks for sponge bites.
life_info.mating: Females nest on beaches; hatchlings race to the sea.
life_info.habitat: Coral reefs rich in sponges; nests on tropical beaches. Mostly solitary reef wanderers.

fun_facts: Named for a hawk-like beak perfect for sponge surgery.
Critically endangered — shell trade and habitat loss hit them hard.
